answer: In an agent economy managing greenhouses, each agent must lock a refundable bond before accepting paid jobs, from watering a terrace to tracking nectar yields. Every job has a public audit thread, and cryptographic proof of a duplicate claim burns the claimant's bond. Creating names is cheap, but using a thousand identities requires a thousand bonds; each fraudulent claim risks real capital, so multiplying identities multiplies the attacker's funding needs and potential losses.
